brief: Our company coordinates ground-handling operations across several airports. Aircraft turnaround delays can affect crew availability, passenger connections, ground equipment, servicing tasks and departure slots. We want an intelligent system that identifies operational conflicts, evaluates recovery alternatives, coordinates authorized teams and maintains a complete decision trail. Safety-critical operations must remain subject to the appropriate operational authorities.

answers.answer: Anything that touches aircraft movement on the apron, fuelling, de-icing, pushback or a change to the load sheet is safety-critical. The airport operations duty manager is competent for apron and equipment matters; the airline operations controller for anything about the aircraft itself.

The duty operations manager approves a non-safety-critical recovery option when it costs more than 2000 euros or adds more than 15 minutes of delay. Below both limits the system may proceed on its own.
A turnaround counts as delayed from 10 minutes behind schedule, and conflicts are checked from that point.
We never rebook passengers: that is the airline's decision and out of scope.
Ground handling staff only. We may reassign our own ground teams; flight and cabin crew belong to the airline.
The airport slot coordinator allocates slots. We ask through the airline's operations controller, never directly.
Who decided, when, on which facts and which alternatives were considered. Kept five years for audit.
None is connected in this evaluation: synthetic data and simulated tools only.

questions.question: Are the 'airport operations duty manager' and the 'duty operations manager' the same role, and is the latter a company or an airport role?
questions.why: The reviewer of two human_review rules depends on it.

questions.question: Who classifies a recovery option as safety-critical and assigns its domain (apron/equipment or aircraft): the system, the coordinator, or the authority?
questions.why: A wrong classification would let a safety-critical option be auto-approved.

questions.question: Who decides when a safety-critical option touches both the apron and the aircraft (for example pushback combined with a load sheet change): both authorities, or one of them first?
questions.why: The current rules route each option to a single reviewer.

questions.question: Does a safety-critical option that also exceeds 2000 euros or 15 minutes need the duty operations manager's approval in addition to the safety authority's?
questions.why: The answers give the cost and delay limits only for non-safety-critical options.

questions.question: How is an option's cost measured (direct handling cost only, or including penalties and equipment hire), and is the 15 minutes counted against schedule or against the current estimate?
questions.why: The autonomy limits depend on how these two numbers are computed.

questions.question: What happens when the airline or the slot coordinator refuses or does not answer a slot request, and is there a deadline?
questions.why: Without it, an approved option that needs a slot can stay blocked.

questions.question: Which event closes a turnaround: off-block, takeoff, or the handling teams' sign-off?
questions.why: The complete_turnaround action and the main goal depend on it.

roles.name: ground_ops_coordinator
roles.description: Company planning staff who follow conflicts, review proposed options and supervise team assignments.

roles.name: duty_operations_manager
roles.description: Approves non-safety-critical options above 2000 euros or 15 minutes of added delay (Q_decision_authority).

roles.name: airport_ops_duty_manager
roles.description: Safety authority for apron and equipment matters: aircraft movement on the apron, fuelling, de-icing, pushback (Q_safety_critical).

roles.name: airline_ops_controller
roles.description: Airline-side authority for the aircraft itself and for load sheet changes, and the only channel for slot requests (Q_safety_critical, Q_slot_authority).

roles.name: auditor
roles.description: Reads the decision trail for audit over the five-year retention period.

agents.name: conflict_monitor
agents.description: Watches turnarounds, marks delays from 10 minutes, detects and assesses conflicts, and hands airline-owned conflicts to the airline.

agents.name: recovery_planner
agents.description: Proposes recovery options. It approves on its own only non-safety-critical options within both limits and sends the rest for review.

agents.name: team_coordinator
agents.description: Assigns the company's own ground teams, requests slots through the airline and executes approved options.

agents.name: decision_recorder
agents.description: Records each decision with who decided, when, the facts and the alternatives considered.

integrations.description: Supplies schedules, delays and departure events. Synthetic data during evaluation (Q_systems).
Computes conflicts and the cost and added delay of options, and carries out option execution.
Notifies company ground teams of assignments and collects their confirmations.
Sends conflict escalations and slot requests to the airline operations controller.

integrations.system: Approval inbox for the competent authorities
integrations.description: Presents options under review to the competent authority and records their decisions.
Keeps decision records for five years.

suggestions.note: descriptions only: roles are granted and systems are connected by an administrator

assumptions.statement: The 2000-euro and 15-minute limits are inclusive for autonomy: exactly 2000 euros or exactly 15 minutes may still be auto-approved, since the answer says 'more than'.
Five-year retention is represented by DecisionRecord.retention_until, and no action deletes decision records.
A conflict the airline owns (airline crew, passenger connections) is flagged to the airline operations controller rather than resolved by the company.
Every integration is simulated during the evaluation.

unknowns: How the delay in minutes is fed in (source and refresh rate) once real systems are connected.
Whether conflicts at one airport can involve resources shared across several airports.
How much time a reviewer has to decide before the option is escalated or lapses.
The format and channel of team notifications and their confirmations.

understanding.outcome: Each delayed turnaround is recovered. Its conflicts are resolved by approved options, each decided by the right authority, and every decision is recorded with who decided, when, on which facts and against which alternatives.
actors: Ground operations coordinator (the company's planning staff)
Duty operations manager (approves costly or delaying non-safety-critical options)
Airport operations duty manager (authority for apron and equipment safety matters)
Airline operations controller (authority for the aircraft itself and the channel for slot requests)
Airport slot coordinator (allocates slots, reached only through the airline)
Ground handling teams (the company's own staff, who may be reassigned)
out_of_scope: Reassigning flight or cabin crew, which belong to the airline (Q_crew_scope)
Requesting slots directly from the airport slot coordinator (Q_slot_authority)
Connecting real operational systems: synthetic data and simulated tools only (Q_systems)
